metaData.originalTitle: Building an Evaluation Harness for Production AI Agents: A 12-Metric Framework From 100+ Deployments
metaData.title: Building an Evaluation Harness for Production AI Agents: A 12-Metric Framework From 100+ Deployments
metaData.oneSentenceSummary: This article presents a comprehensive 12-metric evaluation framework for production AI agents, distilled from over 100 enterprise deployments, covering retrieval, generation, agent behavior, and production health.
metaData.summary: The article argues that evaluation infrastructure, not model quality, is the key differentiator for successful production AI agents. It introduces a 12-metric framework organized into four categories: Retrieval (Context Relevance, Recall, Precision, Latency), Generation (Answer Faithfulness, Answer Relevance, Hallucination Rate), Agent-Specific (Tool Selection Accuracy, Tool Execution Success, Multi-Step Coherence), and Production (Cost per Query, P99 Latency). For each metric, the author defines what it measures, why it matters, how to measure it, and a critical threshold. The article provides a phased implementation roadmap, compares the framework to existing tools like Ragas and LangSmith, and discusses common pitfalls. It emphasizes that teams should build evaluation infrastructure before shipping to production to avoid costly retrofits and trust damage.
metaData.featuredReason: A compliance officer at a healthcare client asked the question the team couldn't answer: How do you know your agent isn't hallucinating patient symptoms? Six weeks later, they shipped — only after wiring up a 12-metric eval harness. Across 100+ enterprise deployments since, that framework now spans retrieval (Context Relevance > 0.85, Hallucination < 2%), generation, and agent behavior, each metric with a measurement method, threshold rationale, and production notes. If you're about to push an agent into the real world, print this before you ship.

mainPoints.point: Evaluation infrastructure is the key differentiator for successful production AI agents, not model quality.
mainPoints.explanation: The author argues that models are commodities, but a robust evaluation framework that catches failures in retrieval, generation, and agent behavior is what separates successful deployments from failures.

mainPoints.point: The framework consists of 12 metrics across four categories: Retrieval, Generation, Agent-Specific, and Production.
mainPoints.explanation: Each category answers a different question about agent performance. Retrieval metrics ensure the agent has the right context; Generation metrics ensure the output is faithful and relevant; Agent metrics ensure multi-step logic is correct; Production metrics ensure the system is cost-effective and fast.

mainPoints.point: Teams should build evaluation infrastructure before shipping to production to avoid costly retrofits.
mainPoints.explanation: The article identifies three common patterns of failure: delaying evaluation until after MVP, relying solely on accuracy, and depending on manual spot-checks. Building the eval harness upfront prevents trust damage and saves 4-6 weeks of retrofit work.

mainPoints.point: Answer Faithfulness and Hallucination Rate are the most critical metrics for regulated industries.
mainPoints.explanation: For healthcare, fintech, and legal use cases, the author recommends a faithfulness threshold of >0.95 and a hallucination rate of <0.5%. These metrics directly determine compliance and user trust.

mainPoints.point: A phased implementation approach is recommended, starting with retrieval and faithfulness metrics.
mainPoints.explanation: Phase 1 (pre-launch) focuses on context relevance, recall, precision, and faithfulness. Phase 2 (soft launch) adds hallucination rate, answer relevance, and tool selection. Phase 3 (stable production) adds cost, latency, and agent-specific metrics.

keyQuotes: The teams shipping AI agents successfully in 2026 aren't the ones with the best models. They're the ones with the best evaluation infrastructure. Models are commodities. Evaluation is differentiation.
If you retrieve 10 chunks and only 3 are relevant, you've polluted the context and forced the model to filter signal from noise.
Faithfulness drops usually indicate one of three causes: temperature settings too high, context window overflow, or prompt template encouraging extrapolation.
Average latency hides the failure modes that frustrate users. A system with 1-second average latency but 15-second p99 has users abandoning sessions after 4-5 slow responses.
LLM-as-judge evaluation costs roughly 30-50% of your inference cost... The ROI is preventing a single production incident that would cost engineer-weeks to debug.
